newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - St George says no Advance talks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - St George says no Advance talks.

text.p: The chairman of St George Bank Ltd, Keith Moremon, said on Thursday that a merger with Advance Bank Ltd made sense but talks had not been held.

"It would make sense too but we have grown organically...extremely well in the past four years since we became a bank and in the 10 years I have been on the board it has been phenomenal growth," Moremon told Reuters.

He said comments in July by Advance chairman Jim Service that a merger of the two regional banks, which are both based in Sydney with strong mortgage portfolios, had "obvious logic" should be construed merely as a general observation.
Asked if he had subsequently spoken to Service about a merger, Moremon said: "I haven't, no. And I don't think anyone else has."

The chairman, who retires from the board at the end of September after six years in that position, said St George was performing well and this had attracted National Australia Bank Ltd onto the register.

"Things are really tough at the moment in the business because of the squeeze on margins and things like that," he said, after a news conference to announce the listing of an entertainment company in which he is also chairman.
"But St George is going extremely well and it is still growing very well organically."
Moremon said he was not personally concerned by the presence of NAB on the share register with a stake of 6.8 percent.

"I think it is just a strategic investment because with the Wallis Inquiry coming up you never know what is going to come out of that. They just want to be in a position where they can deal with the best regional bank in Australia."
The Wallis Inquiry will consider the issue of across-the-board financial industry mergers. Its report is due to be handed to the national government in March next year.
